sentences.text: A miller had three sons.
When he died, the oldest got the mill, the second got a donkey, and the youngest got only a cat.
The youngest son felt very sad.
"What can I do with just a cat?" he said.
Then the Cat said, "Do not worry.
Give me a bag and a pair of boots.
I will help you."
The son was not sure, but he had seen the Cat do many clever tricks before.
He began to feel hopeful and agreed.
The Cat put on his boots and went to the woods.
He put some food in his bag and lay down as if he were dead.
Soon, a young rabbit came to look inside the bag.
The Cat quickly pulled the string, caught it, and went to the King's palace.
The Cat bowed and said, "This is a gift from Lord Carabas."
The King was very pleased with the gift.
Another day, the Cat caught two birds in the same way.
He brought them to the King and said, "These are from Lord Carabas."
For many days, the Cat brought more animals to the King.
The King began to like the Lord Carabas and gave the Cat some gold.
One day, the King went for a ride by the river.
The Cat said, "Master, today your fortune will change.
Come with me to the river."
The young man followed him.
"Go into the water," said the Cat.
While his master was bathing, the Cat hid his clothes under a stone.
Soon the King's coach came by.
The Cat cried, "Help!
The Lord Carabas is drowning!
Thieves stole his clothes!"
The King's guards pulled the young man from the water.
The King gave him fine clothes.
He looked very handsome, and the Princess liked him at once.
The King asked him to join them in the coach.
Meanwhile, the Cat ran ahead and met some workers cutting grass.
"If the King asks," he said, "tell him this land belongs to the Lord Carabas."
The King passed and asked, "Whose land is this?"
"The Lord Carabas's!" the worker answered.
The King was impressed.
He believed that the Lord was a very wealthy man.
The Cat went on and told more workers the same thing.
He did this in fields of grain and across the wide countryside.
So everywhere the King looked, people said the land belonged to the Lord.
At last, the Cat came to a grand castle.
A rich Giant lived there, and all the lands the Cat had just passed by belonged to him.
The Giant had the power to change his shape.
The Cat said, "I heard you can turn into any animal."
"That is true,"answered the Giant.
At once, he became a huge lion.
The Cat quickly jumped back in fear.
Then the Cat said, "That is amazing!
But can you turn into something very small, like a mouse?"
The Giant laughed and turned into a tiny mouse to show off.
The Cat jumped on the mouse.
Now the grand castle belonged to his lord.
The King arrived and was impressed by the castle.
"You are very rich, Lord Carabas," he said.
Lord Carabas married the Princess that very day.
The Cat became a great lord and lived happily ever after.

responseRubric.recommendedActionKo: 다음 이야기로 이동하거나 사건의 원인과 결과를 말로 설명합니다.

responseRubric.definitionKo: 핵심 정보는 파악했지만 순서·관계·세부 단서의 일부가 불완전합니다.

principles: Story Grammar structures what is assessed but is not treated as the sole model of reading comprehension.
Scores reflect evidence of Story Element and relationship understanding, not lexical or semantic similarity alone.
100/67/33/0 are operational reporting values; they are not empirically calibrated IRT ability estimates.
